options.content:
CPU, memory, disk, database connections, Valkey memory, Qdrant collection size, object-storage usage and worker concurrency are served by **node_exporter, cAdvisor, postgres_exporter, redis_exporter, Qdrant's own /metrics and SeaweedFS**. They are deliberately **not** re-exported under `kb_` — two numbers for one fact disagree during exactly the incident you need them for. See `infrastructure/observability/exporters/README.md`.

Those panels are missing from this dashboard for two concrete reasons, both fixable and neither cosmetic:

1. **The scrape targets are unreachable today.** The `observability` network is `internal: true` and Prometheus is the only member that needs to reach `data`. Every exporter must join **both** networks before a single `node_*` or `pg_*` series exists.
2. **The CI catalog gate compares dashboard metric names against the closed `kb_*` catalog.** Until that gate learns the exporter families as a second permitted name source, a panel querying `node_memory_MemAvailable_bytes` fails the build.

An empty dashboard is honest. A panel with a plausible-looking metric name that nothing emits is a green gate over a permanently blank graph.

panels.title: Running builds
panels.description: The _info pattern: the value is always 1 and carries nothing, the labels carry everything. git_sha is the one permitted high-churn label value in the entire catalog, which is exactly why it is confined to a single always-1 gauge — one series per running build, replaced on deployment.

panels.title: Dependency up (0/1)
panels.description: What /health/ready decided, per dependency, with `required` alongside. The six dependency values are fixed: postgres, valkey, qdrant, object_storage, ai_api, core_api. `embedding` and `reranker` were removed by ADR-030 and are not coming back — both are provider API calls now, readiness must never probe an external provider, and no process can emit either series. A per-org provider credential is NOT a dependency either: per-credential breaker state is per-tenant data and lives in PostgreSQL, surfaced on the admin dashboard. A reranking capability gap shows on the Retrieval dashboard as kb_retrieval_rerank_skips_total, not here. Optional dependencies at 0 are degraded, not failing, and open a ticket after 15 minutes (KbOptionalDependencyDown).

panels.title: Circuit breaker state (0 closed, 1 half-open, 2 open)
panels.description: The breaker is invisible without this series. Open for more than 5 minutes pages (KbCircuitBreakerOpen). Half-open is the breaker working — it admits at most 3 concurrent probes and closes only after 3 consecutive successes — and is never alerted on.

panels.title: Scheduler freshness by task (seconds since last tick)
panels.description: Layer 1 of three. The gauge is exported by core-api from a PostgreSQL row SEEDED IN THE MIGRATION, not by the scheduler container, which has no scrape target of its own — a scheduler that never started after a deployment must read as an ancient timestamp rather than a missing series, because a series that never existed cannot be threshold-alerted. Pages above 900 s (KbSchedulerStalled).

panels.title: Scheduled task runs by task and outcome
panels.description: The only family where outcome may be `skipped`. A skip is the withoutOverlapping lock working, so it sits outside the error rate — but sustained skips are the fingerprint of a lock stranded by SIGKILL, whose default TTL is 24 hours, during which the freshness gauge above stays perfectly green while no work happens (KbSchedulerSkipStuck).

panels.title: Sources overdue for recrawl
panels.description: Layer 3. Counted from PostgreSQL by the API on scrape, deliberately not by the scheduler: it is the only signal that catches a scheduler ticking perfectly while the work does not happen — a stranded lock, a wedged queue, a dispatcher that claims and throws.

panels.title: Internal seam requests by operation and status_class
panels.description: The Laravel-to-FastAPI seam itself, keyed on the X-KB-Operation header and NEVER on the URL path — a path is unbounded once it carries an identifier. This is the panel that distinguishes 'the AI service is failing' from 'we cannot reach the AI service'.

panels.title: Internal seam requests by operation and error_class
panels.description: The same counter split by taxonomy class rather than status. internal_dependency here means the seam itself is down; anything else is the data plane reporting a classified failure through it.
